summary: Reviewed all artifact files and generated output for the complete persona model-field rework. All 4 review dimensions pass with no blocking issues found.

YAML changes (WP-001): _shared.yaml `default_model: 'Claude Sonnet 4.6'` properly placed with inline comment. 1-planner.yaml and 2-project-manager.yaml have `model: 'Claude Opus 4.6'` after `role`. Agents 3-7 confirmed to have no `model` field — verified via grep.

Build script changes (WP-002): `!== undefined` guard correctly distinguishes absent fields from falsy values. Fallback chain `persona.model → default_model || cc_model || 'inherit'` is logically correct. `ccModel` derived from resolved `model`, not static passthrough. Computed `model` and `cc_model` placed AFTER `...persona` spread — correctly prevents clobbering.

Template change (WP-002): `model: '{{model}}'` added to FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_VSCODE after `description`, using single quotes for YAML safety. No changes to ccFrontmatterFields() or FRONTMATTER_LEDGER_CC — correct.

Manifest docs (WP-003): api-surface.md, data-flows.md, and constraints.md all updated. Resolution chains documented accurately. Constraints 26b and 26c clearly document the default_model + per-persona override pattern and the cc_model resolution chain.

Generated output verified: Agent 1 (Planner) → `model: 'Claude Opus 4.6'` in both VS Code and Claude Code; Agent 3 (Developer) → `model: 'Claude Sonnet 4.6'` in both targets. All 7 ledger personas deployed correctly.

Standalone regression confirmed: Claude Code standalone retains `model: 'inherit'` via the cc_model fallback chain (no default_model in standalone _shared.yaml). VS Code standalone has no model field — correct.

comments.note: Minor documentation precision gap in data-flows.md: Layer 3 comments use `??` notation (e.g. `persona.model ?? ...`) while the code uses `!== undefined` ternary. In practice these are equivalent since YAML never yields null for missing fields, but technically `??` passes null while `!== undefined` blocks it. Non-blocking — just a notation alignment opportunity for a future documentation pass.

validateLedgerVSCodeFrontmatter() (constraint 31) does not yet validate the new `model` field in VS Code ledger personas — it only checks `role`, `name`, and `vs_file_name`. The CC validator already checks `model`. Adding a model check to the VS Code validator would catch accidental omission of the field in future template changes. Non-blocking given that validation is advisory anyway.

summary: Reviewed all documentation artifacts across WP-001 through WP-005 for outstanding gaps. Changelog (v3.7.3) and manifest docs (api-surface.md, data-flows.md, constraints.md) were already updated in WP-003. Addressed two low-priority notation/accuracy gaps flagged by the Reviewer.

data-flows.md: Fixed Layer 3 comments for `model` and `cc_model` — replaced `??` shorthand notation with the accurate `!== undefined` ternary form that matches the actual build script code. The distinction matters because `??` passes null while `!== undefined` blocks it; YAML never yields null for absent fields (making them equivalent in practice), but the docs now precisely reflect the implementation.

constraints.md constraint 31: Updated to name the function `validateVSCodeFrontmatter()`, add `id` to the verified field list (the code has checked `id` since v3.7.0 but constraint 31 didn't mention it), and document that `model` is not yet validated by the VS Code ledger validator — explicitly flagging the known gap without blocking sync.

comments.note: Constraint 31 was doubly stale: (1) it omitted `id` which was added to validateVSCodeFrontmatter() in v3.7.0, and (2) it didn't mention `model` (added in v3.7.3) is absent from VS Code validation. Both gaps corrected in this pass.

The `version` comment in data-flows.md Layer 3 also uses `??` notation (predates this project). Left untouched per implementation discipline — not in scope and the semantic difference is equally irrelevant there (YAML absent fields are never null).
